• The chart's Grafana dashboards load with auto-refresh off, so an open dashboard does not re-query its datasources on a timer; refresh by hand or pick an interval.
  • Enterprise observability counts a generation's whole input under both Langfuse usage conventions (input with or without cache reads and writes): the Overview's uncached input ratio is no longer negative, its cache-read share stays at or below 100%, and sessions, traces, workloads, classification and the cost cache comparison stop undercounting input.
  • platform-api presents a user's Dex refresh token once per refresh. A refused refresh was sent to Dex twice, which Dex can read as token reuse and which then ended every session of that user.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A rollout no longer cuts open requests after 10 s: gateway, forwarder and platform-api leave their Service before stopping (shutdown.drainSeconds, default 10) and let open requests finish for up to shutdown.timeoutSeconds (default 120, ACH_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT).
  • platform-api has a readiness probe on /readyz, so it gets no traffic before Postgres and Valkey answer.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• ach migrate never prints the database URL or password: a DSN that does not parse fails with a fixed message and driver errors are scrubbed. Percent-encode special characters in the password (see the ach-install prerequisites).
  • ach-cli no longer sends x-ach-key to a different origin on a redirect.
  • The http source no longer forwards its Secret-valued header across a cross-host redirect.
  • ach-cli local plugin install and uninstall never widen the mode of an existing file: a 0600 runtime config stays 0600.
  • The forwarder drops a client tags header: only ACH sets request tags, on every route.
  • The forwarder refuses a multipart body whose Content-Type repeats boundary or carries a starred boundary* with 400 invalid_request.
  • An archive that fills its extraction cap exactly no longer lifts the cap for the entries after it; prompt archives share the skill cap.
  • The console login next= refuses control characters, so a browser cannot normalise it to another origin.
  • Release images are signed by digest, not by tag.
  • ach-cli local plugin|skill install, update and uninstall refuse a project destination that leaves the folder through a symlink, as env hydrate does; --global is unchanged.
  • A BackendIdentityPolicy consentAudience of ach, ach-ek, or starting with mcp: or a2a: is refused at admission, and the consent login skips the broker hop for such a value already stored.
  • A private-repo token reaches git through its environment, not its command line (needs git 2.31 or later for ach-cli local).

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• The operator no longer looks up or deletes an Environment's access group under the names ach-<env> or <env>; only ach-env-<env> is used.
  • OpenWork and its Den API: the openwork.* chart values and the /openwork, /api/den routes are gone, and the console bootstrap no longer carries openwork_enabled.

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text: • An install on v0.6.19 or earlier that jumps straight to this release leaves each Environment's old access group (named ach-<env> or <env>) in LiteLLM, orphaned and still bound to its teams; delete it by hand. Installs that ran any later release are unaffected.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Docs, the console and the e2e suite follow LiteLLM v1.108's budget refusal: HTTP 422 with type: budget_exceeded, not 429. ACH keeps that default because clients stop at once and show why, instead of retrying a request that cannot succeed. The e2e LiteLLM pin moves to v1.108.1.
  • scripts/dev.sh shares one Go build and module cache per machine, Go's own defaults, so a new worktree starts warm. Existing .gocache/build and .gocache/gopath/pkg directories can be deleted with make clean-cache.
  • make cluster-up and make e2e-run refuse to start with under 5 GB free on the workspace disk.
  • ACH requires LiteLLM 1.108 or later.
  • The forwarder refuses request bodies on /v1, /gemini and /a2a that set a LiteLLM per-request control (api_key, deployment_id, guardrail fields, mcp tools) with 400 client_param_not_allowed. Form bodies refuse the same top-level names.
  • /gemini serves only the model routes (GET /v1beta/models[/{model}] and POST /v1beta/models/{model}:{generateContent|streamGenerateContent|countTokens|embedContent|batchEmbedContents}); other paths answer 404 route_not_allowed. A body or batch entry model that differs from the path model, or a POST body whose Content-Type is neither application/json nor absent, is 400 model_mismatch.
  • Requests that outlive their key end within about a minute of the key being suspended, revoked or expired, including streams and /v1/realtime.
  • POST /platform/oauth/register answers 413 over 4 KiB and 429 rate_limited past a per-address and a global limit, per replica.
  • ach-cli env hydrate and env uninstall refuse a path in the workspace that resolves outside it (--global is exempt). In --global mode a recorded absolute target must sit under the tool's config root.
  • While an Environment has unresolved references, the operator applies removals only: access can shrink, nothing is added.
  • POST /platform/admin/users/{email}/revoke-keys normalises the email, walks every page of keys and answers 500 if a page fails; rerun it to finish. It ends the user's OAuth sessions once, with or without an active pk_, and answers 500 if that fails, after sweeping the keys; rerun it to end them.
  • Ending a user's OAuth sessions also invalidates refresh tokens issued before a later login.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Writing a content CR or a LiteLLMConnection is equivalent to reading every Secret in the ACH namespace; give such writers admin-tier trust.
  • A user disabled at the IdP keeps working ek- keys; offboard with ach-cli admin keys revoke --owner <email>.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • A killed make no longer leaves its ach-devtools container running.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Agent keys get the backend identity JWT: on an /mcp or /a2a target with a forwardIdentityJWT policy, an ek_ arrives as its owner, with the same sub, email and groups as the owner's pk_, plus an azp claim (ek:<environment>) for audit. MCP backends no longer need the LiteLLM key, which LiteLLM v1.106+ stops forwarding.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Releases go through a PR: make release-cut opens it with the rotated CHANGELOG and manifest bumps, and the merged commit is what gets tagged. GitHub release notes are that version's CHANGELOG section.
  • The OpenCode bootstrap skill (<provider>-ach) loads on any mention of an Environment and installs a named one, instead of leaving agents to search the disk for it.
  • The OpenCode bootstrap skill and the ach-cli plugin (1.1.4) give agents a background recipe for MCP sign-in, so they hand over the link instead of hanging the session on the browser wait.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • GET /v2/model/info?model=<alias> returns a row for a LiteLLM model-group alias, with the target model's vision, PDF, token-limit, tool and cost fields. Agents on an alias such as ackstorm.smart no longer lose images from tool results or run unpriced. A name the caller is not granted stays a 403.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • The pre-push git hook, with make pre-push, make hooks and make verify. CI is the gate. Delete .git/hooks/pre-push from existing clones.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Deleting a Plugin, Prompt, Skill, Artifact, BackendIdentityPolicy or LiteLLMConnection now removes its Postgres row too. Plugin, Prompt and Artifact rows left soft-deleted still answered by name; their cached content was already gone.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • The deletion_timestamp column on every table and the deletionTimestamp field of the Environment API view. Migration 000028 purges the remaining soft-deleted rows, then drops the column. Pods from an earlier version fail reads on those tables from the migration until the rollout replaces them. helm rollback below this release leaves them failing until 000028_drop_deletion_timestamp.down.sql is applied by hand.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Breaking for older ach-cli: POST /platform/hydrate now returns runtime.models[].limits ({context, output}) when LiteLLM knows them, aliases resolved. ach-cli decodes this response strictly, so v1.1.2 and older fail with unknown field "limits" until updated. Release this ach-cli first, then upgrade the server. ach-agent ignores the field and keeps working.
  • Console pages use the full width, and Reliability is hidden from the sidebar. The page stays served at /analytics/reliability.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• ach-cli warns on stderr, once per run, when its version differs from the server's. platform-api reports its version in X-ACH-Server-Version on authenticated responses.
  • ach-cli launch without --environment updates every Environment recorded under the folder's .ach/, then starts the tool.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Deleting an Environment now removes its Postgres row. It used to stay soft-deleted forever: gone from env list, but still answering hydrate, env describe, the console and content downloads by name, reported as Available. Migration 000027 purges the rows already left behind.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Console catalogs: MCP cards show the gateway URL, Models lists agents published as models, and an empty A2A or MCP list reads as no grant rather than a disabled gateway.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• ach-cli launch <claude|codex|gemini|opencode|pi> --environment <env> hydrates that one target, then starts the tool in --dir and exits with its code. A missing tool or a failed hydrate starts nothing.
  • ach-cli refresh (POST /platform/refresh): after being added to an SSO group, join the teams it maps to (platformApi.teams.sso/users) without logging in again. It re-reads the groups at the identity provider; the Environments follow at their next reconcile.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• KeyGrant ServiceAccount names are validated as DNS-1123 subdomains.
  • The console's Spend KPI becomes Budget when a cycle exists, plotting that cycle's days. The console range opens on the last 7 days.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• KeyGrant (ach.ackstorm.ai/v1alpha1): a platform admin names one identity, its Environments and the ServiceAccounts (<namespace>/<name>) that may act as it, with an optional per-key budget. The operator projects it, reports Ready (IdentityUnknown, EnvironmentMissing), revokes exchange keys no grant allows any more and keeps each covered key's key:<id> budget at the lowest covering spec.budget.
  • POST /platform/keys/exchange: a pod-bound ServiceAccount token plus a matching grant buys a short-lived ACH JWT (aud: ach-ek) standing for one stable ek_ per identity, Environment and ServiceAccount; the ek_ never leaves ACH. The token's signature is verified against the cluster JWKS before any rate limiting or TokenReview. The JWT lifetime is platformApi.keyExchange.tokenTTL (default 15m, 1m to 1h). The forwarder, content service and platform API accept the JWT wherever an ek_ goes. Every exchange emits a platform.ek.exchange audit event.
  • Helm: platform-api system:auth-delegator binding (TokenReview); ClusterRole <release>-keygrant-editor (create, update, patch, delete on keygrants), bound to nobody.
  • Plugin marketplace ach at the repo root (Claude Code and Codex) with three plugins: ach-cli (using the platform from the CLI), ach-gitops (writing ACH custom resources) and ach-install (deploying the Helm chart). Install with claude plugin marketplace add ackstorm/ach, or serve them to users through a PluginMarketplace and an Environment.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• platform-api now holds a cluster-wide system:auth-delegator ClusterRoleBinding (it held no Kubernetes privilege before) and relies on the default system:service-account-issuer-discovery binding to read the cluster JWKS.
  • The API-server audit level for tokenreviews must be Metadata; Request or RequestResponse would log the submitted ServiceAccount tokens.
  • Operator RBAC for keygrants: get, list, watch, update, plus keygrants/finalizers and keygrants/status; never create, delete or patch.
  • Exchange keys do not count against max_keys.
  • Owner budget changes on exchange keys are refused (409 budget_managed_by_grant); the grant's spec.budget is the only source.
  • Migration 000026 adds environment_keys.issued_via and requester and the key_grants table; its down step refuses while live exchange keys exist.
  • The ach-gitops and ach-install plugins (1.1.0) gain KeyGrant and key-exchange guidance.
  • The OpenCode onboarding skill (<provider>-ach) is a bootstrap only: install ach-cli, sign in, list Environments, hydrate the default Environment. The rest moved to the ach-cli plugin, which the default Environment should carry.
  • Chart NOTES.txt describes this chart (10 CRDs managed by Helm, the operator creating LiteLLMConnection/default); platformApi.admins is declared in values.yaml; the unused watchNamespace value is gone.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • BackendIdentityPolicy docs: when several policies target the same backend, the alphabetically FIRST one wins (the docs said last).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Console Enterprise Overview: the input statistics (median, maximum, reasoning share, period) sit in the fourth column of the input/output panel again instead of wrapping to a row of their own.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• ACH 1.0.0: the operator, platform API (OAuth 2.1 AS, pk_/ek_ keys, console), forwarder, content service, optional gateway, and the ach-cli user CLI.
  • One container image, ghcr.io/ackstorm/ach. The Enterprise features (conversation classification, observability analytics, traces) are enabled with the Helm value enterprise.enabled and need an ACKstorm Enterprise licence agreement for production use; the rest is Apache-2.0.

docs.title: ach-cli command reference
docs.text: Every ach-cli command, as printed by --help.

docs.title: ach-cli
docs.text:
ACH CLI — operator/developer client for the ACH control plane

Usage:
  ach-cli [flags]
  ach-cli [command]

Available Commands:
  admin       Admin operations (inventory, keys, user budgets and limits, refresh)
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  environment Inspect environments visible to the active credential
  help        Help about any command
  keys        Manage your environment keys (ek-…)
  launch      Start the agent tool, hydrating an Environment first when asked
  local       Local, ungoverned developer package path (repo/plugin/skill)
  login       Sign in to a Hub (browser on this machine, or a code from any browser)
  logout      Sign out of the active profile
  profile     Manage your profiles (~/.config/ach/config.yaml)
  refresh     Re-read your identity provider groups and update your access
  token       Print the active profile's token, or its key (credential helper)
  upgrade     Replace this ach-cli with the latest release
  whoami      Show who you are signed in as, your budget and your key allowance

Flags:
  -h, --help      help for ach-cli
  -v, --version   version for ach-cli

Use "ach-cli [command] --help" for more information about a command.

docs.title: ach-cli admin
docs.text:
Operator-facing admin surface. Every subcommand requires a signed-in
session (`ach-cli login`) of a platform admin: an email in the Helm value
`platformApi.admins.users`, or a member of a group in
`platformApi.admins.sso`. Environment keys (ek-) are refused. Other
callers receive `403 not_admin` and the CLI exits 3.

Usage:
  ach-cli admin [flags]
  ach-cli admin [command]

Available Commands:
  keys        Admin key operations
  list        List ACH objects and the LiteLLM runtime catalog (read-only)
  refresh     Force-refresh an external content resource
  users       Set a user's budget or limits

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for admin

Use "ach-cli admin [command] --help" for more information about a command.

docs.title: ach-cli admin keys
docs.text:
Admin key operations

Usage:
  ach-cli admin keys [flags]
  ach-cli admin keys [command]

Available Commands:
  list        List every key (pk- and ek-) across owners
  revoke      Revoke one key by id (pkid_… or ekid_…), or every key an owner holds

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for keys

Use "ach-cli admin keys [command] --help" for more information about a command.

docs.title: ach-cli admin keys list
docs.text:
List every key (pk- and ek-) across owners

Usage:
  ach-cli admin keys list [flags]

Examples:
  ach-cli admin keys list --owner alice@example.com --status suspended

Flags:
      --cursor string        Pagination cursor
      --environment string   Filter by environment (ek- only)
  -h, --help                 help for list
      --key string           Authenticate with an environment key (ek-…)
      --limit int            Max rows per page
  -o, --output string        Output format: table|json (default "table")
      --owner string         Filter by owner email
      --profile string       Use this profile instead of the active one
      --status string        Filter by status: active|suspended|revoked|expired|all (default "active")
      --type string          Filter by type: pk|ek
      --verbose              Dump request headers to stderr (credentials redacted)

docs.title: ach-cli admin keys revoke
docs.text:
Revoke one key by id (pkid_… or ekid_…), or every key an owner holds

Usage:
  ach-cli admin keys revoke [<key-id> | --owner <email>] [flags]

Examples:
  ach-cli admin keys revoke ekid_01H…
  ach-cli admin keys revoke --owner alice@example.com --yes

Flags:
  -h, --help             help for revoke
      --key string       Authenticate with an environment key (ek-…)
      --owner string     Revoke every key (pk- and ek-) this email owns
      --profile string   Use this profile instead of the active one
      --verbose          Dump request headers to stderr (credentials redacted)
      --yes              Bypass interactive confirmation

docs.title: ach-cli admin list
docs.text:
Read-only inventory. Admin-only.

ACH objects (from the Postgres projections, version + sync status):
  environments, plugins, prompts, artifacts, skills, marketplaces,
  skill-marketplaces, bips
LiteLLM runtime catalog (KIND NAME STATUS):
  models, mcp, a2a, teams, guardrails
'all' fans out across every kind.

PLUGINS merges standalone Plugin CRs (SOURCE=plugin) with plugins discovered
inside marketplaces (SOURCE=marketplace, shown as <name>@<marketplace>).
SKILLS likewise merges standalone Skill CRs (SOURCE=skill) with skills
discovered inside skill-marketplaces (SOURCE=marketplace, <name>@<marketplace>).
MARKETPLACES / SKILL-MARKETPLACES show the marketplace objects themselves
(Synced status + contained count), not their contained plugins/skills.

SYNC column:
  Synced / Degraded(<reason>) / Pending      marketplaces, skill-marketplaces, environments
  fresh / STALE(<age> over) / never          content kinds (refresh staleness)
  projected                                  bips

AVAILABLE column (content kinds): a newer commit on the watched ref of a
source pinned to spec.<git>.commit; promote it in GitOps. '-' when none.

Note: prompts/artifacts show 'fresh*' — their refresh tracks name resolution,
not content presence. plugins and skills are truly content-gated (bare 'fresh').
Guardrails add MODE and DEFAULT-ON columns.

Usage:
  ach-cli admin list <kind|all> [flags]

Examples:
  ach-cli admin list plugins
  ach-cli admin list models -o json
  ach-cli admin list all -o yaml

Flags:
  -h, --help             help for list
      --key string       Authenticate with an environment key (ek-…)
  -o, --output string    Output format: table|json|yaml (default "table")
      --profile string   Use this profile instead of the active one
      --verbose          Dump request headers to stderr (credentials redacted)

docs.title: ach-cli admin refresh
docs.text:
kind must be one of {plugin, prompt, artifact, skill, marketplace, skill-marketplace}. No interactive confirmation (idempotent operation).

Usage:
  ach-cli admin refresh <kind> <name> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help             help for refresh
      --key string       Authenticate with an environment key (ek-…)
      --profile string   Use this profile instead of the active one
      --verbose          Dump request headers to stderr (credentials redacted)

docs.title: ach-cli admin users
docs.text:
Set a user's budget or limits

Usage:
  ach-cli admin users [flags]
  ach-cli admin users [command]

Available Commands:
  budget      Set a user's total spend ceiling (all their keys and sessions)

Flags:

Use "ach-cli admin users [command] --help" for more information about a command.

docs.title: ach-cli admin users budget
docs.text:
Set the spend ceiling (USD) that covers everything one user spends: their
personal session and every key they own. A user who has never signed in is
created, not refused. A later sign-in never overwrites it.

Usage:
  ach-cli admin users budget <email> [flags]

Examples:
  ach-cli admin users budget alice@example.com --max-budget 200 --budget-duration 30d

Flags:
      --budget-duration string   Budget reset period, e.g. 30d
  -h, --help                     help for budget
      --key string               Authenticate with an environment key (ek-…)
      --max-budget float         Spend ceiling, in USD
      --profile string           Use this profile instead of the active one
      --verbose                  Dump request headers to stderr (credentials redacted)

docs.title: ach-cli admin users limits
docs.text:
Set how many non-revoked keys one user may hold (0 = none). Takes effect on
their next keys create.

Usage:

Examples:
  ach-cli admin users limits alice@example.com --max-keys 10

Flags:

      --profile string   Use this profile instead of the active one
      --verbose          Dump request headers to stderr (credentials redacted)

docs.title: ach-cli environment
docs.text:
Inspect environments visible to the active credential.

environment list + describe are read-only and synthetic-mode friendly.
describe gracefully degrades on 403 unauthorized_team — printing
'(unavailable)' for runtime + context and exiting 0.

Usage:
  ach-cli environment [flags]
  ach-cli environment [command]

Aliases:
  environment, env

Available Commands:
  clone       Create a folder for an Environment and hydrate it (like git clone)
  describe    Show one environment's runtime + context manifest
  fetch       Fetch one content artifact and write its raw bytes to stdout
  hydrate     Install an Environment's content and MCP/A2A config into your agent tool
  list        List environments visible to the active credential
  search      Find plugins, skills, MCP servers and more across your environments
  status      Show what is installed here and whether it is up to date
  uninstall   Remove the projected resource set for the active workspace+environment

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for environment

Use "ach-cli environment [command] --help" for more information about a command.

docs.title: ach-cli environment clone
docs.text:
Create <dir> (default: ./<env>) and hydrate the Environment into it. Refuses
a destination that exists and is not empty. On failure the folder is removed
if clone created it.

To update later: cd <dir> && ach-cli environment hydrate

An empty folder has nothing to autodetect, so --target (or ACH_TARGET) is
required.

Example:
  ach-cli environment clone aws-rw --target claude-code

Usage:
  ach-cli environment clone <env> [dir] [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help             help for clone
      --insecure         Allow a plaintext http:// Hub URL (credentials sent unencrypted; localhost still requires this)
      --key string       Authenticate with an environment key (ek-…)
      --models           Route the tool's model traffic through ACH (apiKeyHelper / model provider wiring)
      --no-warnings      Suppress the tip to use an environment key (ek-) instead of your sign-in
      --only-runtime     Install ONLY runtime entries (skip context)
      --profile string   Use this profile instead of the active one
      --target strings   Agent target(s), comma-separated or repeated: claude-code / codex / gemini-cli / opencode / pi
      --verbose          Dump request headers to stderr (credentials redacted)

docs.title: ach-cli environment describe
docs.text:
Show one environment's runtime + context manifest.

-o json prints {environment, runtime, context}: the environment's name,
namespace, status, description and conditions, then the same runtime and
context lists the table shows. runtime and context are null when the manifest
is unavailable or skipped with --metadata-only.

Usage:
  ach-cli environment describe <name> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help             help for describe
      --key string       Authenticate with an environment key (ek-…)
      --metadata-only    Skip the /platform/hydrate call (faster, env metadata only)
  -o, --output string    Output format: table|json (default "table")
      --profile string   Use this profile instead of the active one
      --verbose          Dump request headers to stderr (credentials redacted)

docs.title: ach-cli environment fetch
docs.text:
Stream a single artifact from the Content Service verbatim (a debug tool).

kind ∈ {prompt, plugin, artifact, skill}. No extraction, no adapter
projection — the response body is written as-is to stdout (or --file).
For normal workspace setup use 'ach-cli environment hydrate'.

The Environment is always sent as x-ach-environment; with an ek- key it
must be the key's own Environment.

Example:
  ach-cli environment fetch frontend-dev plugin code-review --file code-review.tar.gz

Usage:
  ach-cli environment fetch <env> <kind> <name> [flags]

Flags:
      --file string      Write to this file instead of stdout
  -h, --help             help for fetch
      --key string       Authenticate with an environment key (ek-…)
      --profile string   Use this profile instead of the active one
      --verbose          Dump request headers to stderr (credentials redacted)

docs.title: ach-cli environment hydrate
docs.text:
Download an environment's content (prompts, skills, artifacts) into your
agent tool's config directory, and wire up its runtime (MCP / A2A; models
only with --models).

Scope:
  (default)           Project context (prompts / plugins / artifacts /
                      skills) AND runtime (MCP servers / A2A agents).
  --only-runtime      Project ONLY runtime entries (excludes context).
  --only <kind>/<name>
                      Install just one plugin or skill (plugin/<name> or
                      skill/<name>) and merge it into the existing state.
                      No runtime is written; needs an environment and
                      cannot be combined with --sync, --only-runtime.
  --models            Also route the tool's model traffic through ACH
                      (Claude Code apiKeyHelper + ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, Codex
                      model provider; needs ach-cli on PATH). Off by
                      default: the tool keeps its own model login.

Behavior:
  --sync              Remove files no longer in the environment.
  --force             Overwrite local edits and bypass safety refusals.
  --dry-run           Show what would change without writing anything.
  --allow-symlinks    Permit symlinks in downloaded archives (unsafe).
  --conflict <p>      Two plugins writing the same file: namespace (default,
                      prefix with the plugin name) | skip | overwrite | refuse.

Locking:
  --wait              Wait indefinitely if another hydrate holds the lock.
  --lock-timeout <d>  Wait up to <d> (e.g. 30s, 5m). Conflicts with --wait.

Location:
  --dir <dir>         Workspace root (default: current directory).
  -g, --global        Hydrate under $HOME/.ach/<env> instead of ./.ach.
  --target <id[,id…]> Agent target(s): claude-code / codex / gemini-cli /
                      opencode / pi (comma-separated or repeated;
                      ACH_TARGET is the same). Omitted: autodetected from
                      the workspace.

Credentials:
  --key <name|ek-…>   A key saved in the profile, or a raw ek-… key
                      (ACH_KEY is the same). Otherwise the profile's own
                      session (ach-cli login) is used.

The positional <name> is the environment; with a key it is optional (the
key is already scoped to one environment). Without <name>, every environment
already hydrated in this folder (.ach/) is updated with its recorded targets.

Example:
  ach-cli environment hydrate frontend-dev --only plugin/code-review -g --target claude-code

Exit codes:
  0 success   1 usage/credential error   2 local edits would be lost
  3 not authorized   4 wrong environment for this key   5 state mismatch
  6 network error   7 file-name collision   8 config read/write error

Usage:
  ach-cli environment hydrate [env] [flags]

Flags:
      --allow-symlinks          Permit symlinks in downloaded archives (unsafe)
      --conflict string         Cross-plugin collision policy: namespace|skip|overwrite|refuse (default "namespace")
      --dir string              Workspace root override (default: cwd)
      --dry-run                 Run read+diff steps but skip state write and content extract
      --force                   Bypass drift refusal, environment guard, and schema mismatch
  -g, --global                  Use $HOME/.ach/<env> scope instead of cwd/.ach
  -h, --help                    help for hydrate
      --insecure                Allow a plaintext http:// Hub URL (credentials sent unencrypted; localhost still requires this)
      --key string              Authenticate with an environment key (ek-…)
      --lock-timeout duration   Wait up to <d> for workspace lock (mutually exclusive with --wait)
      --models                  Route the tool's model traffic through ACH (apiKeyHelper / model provider wiring)
      --no-warnings             Suppress the tip to use an environment key (ek-) instead of your sign-in
      --only string             Install just one item, plugin/<name> or skill/<name>, merging it into the existing state
      --only-runtime            Reconcile ONLY runtime entries (skip context)
      --profile string          Use this profile instead of the active one
      --sync                    Delete state entries no longer in the environment (deepest-first)
      --target strings          Override platform autodetection; comma-separated or repeated for several targets, e.g. codex,opencode (claude-code / codex / gemini-cli / opencode / pi + case-folded aliases)
      --verbose                 Dump request headers to stderr (credentials redacted)
      --wait                    Block indefinitely on workspace lock contention

docs.title: ach-cli environment status
docs.text:
Show the installed/projected resources recorded in state.json, and whether
each Environment changed since it was hydrated.

By default it prints, per Environment, its targets and scope, the installed
items grouped by kind, and every projected file you edited since the last
hydrate. It then asks the server whether each Environment changed since that
hydrate: "up to date", or + added to the Environment, - removed from it,
~ new content. It downloads nothing. --offline skips the server.

Use --files (-f) to list every projected file with its on-disk TARGET path,
or -o json for machine-readable output; both are local only.

Without [env] (project scope) it lists every hydrated environment; -g
(global scope) requires [env].

An empty or missing state.json prints "No resources installed" (or an
empty JSON array under -o json) and exits 0.

Usage:
  ach-cli environment status [env] [flags]

Flags:
      --dir string       Workspace root override (default: cwd)
  -f, --files            List every projected file instead of a per-resource summary
  -g, --global           Use $HOME/.ach/<env> scope instead of cwd/.ach
  -h, --help             help for status
      --key string       Authenticate with an environment key (ek-…)
      --offline          Show local state only; do not ask the server what changed
  -o, --output string    Output format: table|json (default "table")
      --profile string   Use this profile instead of the active one
      --verbose          Dump request headers to stderr (credentials redacted)

docs.title: ach-cli environment uninstall
docs.text:
Tear down the projected resources ach-cli environment hydrate installed for the
active workspace+environment, reusing the same inverse-merge engine that
hydrate --sync uses. uninstall removes the WHOLE projection in scope, or
one plugin/skill with --only; preview with --dry-run.

The positional <name> is the target Environment — REQUIRED, it namespaces
the <ach-dir> in project and --global scope.

Scope (mirrors hydrate):
  (default)           Remove EVERYTHING hydrate wrote: context (prompts /
                      plugins / artifacts / skills) AND runtime config.
  --only-runtime      Strip ONLY runtime config (MCP servers / A2A agents).
  --only <kind>/<name>
                      Remove just one plugin or skill (plugin/<name> or
                      skill/<name>) installed from this environment.

Co-owned files (.mcp.json, .codex/config.toml, .opencode/opencode.json,
CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md) are inverse-merged: only the engine's keys/marker
blocks are removed; other contributors' and the user's keys survive.
User-edited projected files are preserved unless --force (drift-wins).

Example:
  ach-cli environment uninstall frontend-dev --only plugin/code-review -g

Usage:
  ach-cli environment uninstall <name> [flags]

Flags:
      --dir string              Workspace root override (default: cwd)
      --dry-run                 Print planned removals but write nothing to disk
      --force                   Bypass drift refusal — remove user-edited projected files too
  -g, --global                  Use $HOME/.ach/<env> scope instead of cwd/.ach
  -h, --help                    help for uninstall
      --lock-timeout duration   Wait up to <d> for the workspace lock instead of failing fast
      --only string             Remove just one item, plugin/<name> or skill/<name>
      --only-runtime            Strip ONLY runtime config, leaving context in place

docs.title: ach-cli keys
docs.text:
Manage your environment keys. A key (ek-…) is a long-lived secret scoped to
one Environment — for an agent runtime or a CI job that cannot sign in with a
browser. keys create prints it once; store it in the secret store of whatever
uses it. Every other verb takes the key's name or its ekid_… id.

Usage:
  ach-cli keys [flags]
  ach-cli keys [command]

Available Commands:
  budget      Set a key's spend cap
  create      Create a key for an Environment
  list        List your environment keys
  resume      Resume a suspended key
  revoke      Revoke a key for good
  suspend     Suspend a key (it stops working until resumed)

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for keys

Use "ach-cli keys [command] --help" for more information about a command.

docs.title: ach-cli keys budget
docs.text:
Set the spend cap (USD) of one key, optionally per --budget-duration
(e.g. 30d). The cap applies to that key alone;
your own total budget still applies on top of it.
Takes about 10 seconds to take effect.

Usage:
  ach-cli keys budget <name|id> [flags]

Examples:
  ach-cli keys budget laptop --max-budget 20 --budget-duration 30d

Flags:
      --budget-duration string   Budget reset period, e.g. 30d
  -h, --help                     help for budget
      --key string               Authenticate with an environment key (ek-…)
      --max-budget float         Spend cap for this key, in USD
      --profile string           Use this profile instead of the active one
      --verbose                  Dump request headers to stderr (credentials redacted)

docs.title: ach-cli keys create
docs.text:
Create an environment key (ek-…) named --name (required: what the key is
for, so you and the console can tell keys apart). The key is printed to
stdout exactly once and stored nowhere else: put it in the secret store of
whatever uses it.

-o json prints {name, id, environment, key, expires_at} instead of the bare key.

--expires takes a number of days (90d), a duration (720h) or a date
(2026-12-31T00:00:00Z). --max-budget caps what this key can spend (USD),
optionally per --budget-duration (30d); your own total budget still applies.

Usage:
  ach-cli keys create <environment> [flags]

Examples:
  ach-cli keys create frontend-dev --name laptop --expires 90d
  ach-cli keys create staging --name ci-deploy --max-budget 20 --budget-duration 30d

Flags:
      --budget-duration string   Budget reset period, e.g. 30d (needs --max-budget)
      --expires string           Expiry: 90d, a duration (720h) or an RFC3339 date
  -h, --help                     help for create
      --key string               Authenticate with an environment key (ek-…)
      --max-budget float         Spend cap for this key, in USD
      --name string              What the key is for (required)

docs.title: ach-cli launch
docs.text:
Start the tool in --dir (default: the current directory). With --environment
(or ACH_ENVIRONMENT), that Environment is hydrated for the tool first (same
engine and flags as `ach-cli environment hydrate`);
--update-environments (--update-envs) updates every Environment already
hydrated in that folder (.ach/) for the tool. With neither, the tool starts
as the folder is. If hydrate fails, the tool is not started. ach-cli exits with the tool's exit code.

claude keeps its own Claude login and sends its model traffic through ACH:
launch serves the profile's URL on a local port for as long as claude runs,
adding your ACH sign-in (or --key) to every request. ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and
ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS in your shell are ignored; a Claude settings file
that sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL stops the launch. --models is refused for
claude.

Tools: claude, codex, gemini, opencode, pi

Arguments after <tool> are passed to the tool; put the tool's own flags
after --.

Example:
  ach-cli launch claude --environment frontend-dev
  ach-cli launch claude --profile work -- -c
  ach-cli launch opencode --update-environments
  ach-cli launch codex --environment aws-rw --dir ~/work/infra -- --model ackstorm.smart

Usage:
  ach-cli launch <tool> [-- tool args...] [flags]

Flags:
      --conflict string         Cross-plugin collision policy: namespace|skip|overwrite|refuse (default "namespace")
      --dir string              Workspace root override (default: cwd)
      --environment string      Environment to hydrate before starting the tool (ACH_ENVIRONMENT is the same)
      --force                   Bypass drift refusal, environment guard, and schema mismatch
  -g, --global                  Use $HOME/.ach/<env> scope instead of cwd/.ach
  -h, --help                    help for launch
      --insecure                Allow a plaintext http:// Hub URL (credentials sent unencrypted; localhost still requires this)
      --key string              Authenticate with an environment key (ek-…)
      --lock-timeout duration   Wait up to <d> for workspace lock (mutually exclusive with --wait)
      --models                  Route the tool's model traffic through ACH (apiKeyHelper / model provider wiring)
      --no-warnings             Suppress the tip to use an environment key (ek-) instead of your sign-in
      --only-runtime            Reconcile ONLY runtime entries (skip context)
      --profile string          Use this profile instead of the active one
      --sync                    Delete state entries no longer in the environment (deepest-first)
      --update-environments     Update the Environments already hydrated in the folder (.ach/) before starting the tool (or --update-envs)
      --verbose                 Dump request headers to stderr (credentials redacted)
      --wait                    Block indefinitely on workspace lock contention

docs.title: ach-cli login
docs.text:
Sign in to an ACH Hub.

The CLI is a public OAuth client of the Hub's authorization server. After
the profile-name and URL prompts, on a terminal it asks how to finish:

  1) Open the browser on this machine — the code comes back on a loopback
     redirect, nothing to type.
  2) Another device — the Hub shows a code; open the printed URL in any
     browser, confirm the code, and the CLI picks the login up (RFC 8628
     device grant). This is the way in from an SSH host.
  3) Cancel.

Either way the profile stores a short-lived access token + refresh token;
`ach-cli token` prints a fresh access token for tools' credential
helpers. Nothing key-shaped is printed.

Interactive prompts (skipped when --profile / the URL are given):
  Profile name  DNS-1123 label, e.g. "prod" (suggests "default" on first login)
  URL           https://hub.example.com (http:// needs --insecure / ACH_INSECURE)

The URL is the positional argument, else ACH_URL, else the prompt.
Saved keys (keys create) are kept when you log in again.

With ACH_URL and ACH_KEY both set (synthetic mode) login exits 1.

Usage:
  ach-cli login [url] [flags]

Examples:
  ach-cli login https://hub.example.com
  ach-cli login https://hub.example.com --profile prod --no-browser

Flags:
  -h, --help             help for login
      --insecure         Allow a plaintext http:// Hub URL (credentials sent unencrypted; localhost still requires this)
      --no-browser       Show a code to enter in a browser on another device; do not open a browser here
      --no-warnings      Suppress file-mode warnings to stderr
      --profile string   Profile name to write (DNS-1123 label)

docs.title: ach-cli logout
docs.text:
Sign out of the active profile: its session (and machine key, if it has
one) is removed from ~/.config/ach/config.yaml; the URL stays. Keys made
with keys create keep working until you revoke them (ach-cli keys revoke).

With ACH_URL and ACH_KEY both set (synthetic mode) logout exits 1.

Usage:
  ach-cli logout [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help             help for logout
      --profile string   Sign out of this profile instead of the active one

docs.title: ach-cli profile
docs.text:
Manage the profiles in ~/.config/ach/config.yaml. A profile is a Hub URL
plus a credential: an OAuth session from ach-cli login, or a machine key
(ek-…) from ach-cli profile add.

With ACH_URL and ACH_KEY both set (synthetic mode) every verb exits 1.

Usage:
  ach-cli profile [flags]
  ach-cli profile [command]

Available Commands:
  add         Add a machine profile that signs in with a key (no browser)
  list        List profiles (* marks the default)
  remove      Delete a profile (--force for the default one)
  rename      Rename a profile (keeps its credential)
  show        Show one profile (a machine profile's key masked unless --reveal)
  use         Make <name> the default profile

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for profile

Use "ach-cli profile [command] --help" for more information about a command.

docs.title: ach-cli profile add
docs.text:
Add a profile that authenticates with an environment key (ek-…) instead
of an OAuth session — for CI and agent boxes where a browser login is not
possible. Make the key with ach-cli keys create on a signed-in machine.

The first profile added becomes the default; --default makes this one the
default anyway. --force overwrites a profile of the same name.

Usage:
  ach-cli profile add <name> --url <url> --key <ek-…> [flags]

Examples:
  ach-cli profile add ci --url https://hub.example.com --key ek-…

Flags:
      --default      Make this the default profile
      --force        Overwrite an existing profile of the same name
  -h, --help         help for add
      --insecure     Allow a plaintext http:// Hub URL (the key travels unencrypted)
      --key string   The environment key (ek-…) this profile signs in with
      --url string   Hub URL (https://; http:// needs --insecure)

docs.title: ach-cli profile list
docs.text:
List profiles (* marks the default)

Usage:
  ach-cli profile list [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help            help for list
  -o, --output string   Output format: table|json (default "table")

docs.title: ach-cli profile remove
docs.text:
Delete a profile (--force for the default one)

Usage:
  ach-cli profile remove <name> [flags]

Flags:
      --force   Allow removing the default profile
  -h, --help    help for remove

docs.title: ach-cli profile rename
docs.text:
Rename a profile (keeps its credential)

Usage:
  ach-cli profile rename <old> <new> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for rename

docs.title: ach-cli profile show
docs.text:
Show one profile (a machine profile's key masked unless --reveal)

Usage:

Flags:

docs.title: ach-cli refresh
docs.text:
Ask the Hub to re-read your identity at the identity provider and join the
teams your current SSO groups map to, without a browser. Run it after being
added to a group, instead of logging in again.

Environments follow at their next reconcile (a few minutes). Teams are only
added, never removed. Needs a login session (ach-cli login), not a key.

Exit codes: 0 success, 3 not authorized (log in again), 6 network error.

Usage:
  ach-cli refresh [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help             help for refresh
      --key string       Authenticate with an environment key (ek-…)
      --profile string   Use this profile instead of the active one
      --verbose          Dump request headers to stderr (credentials redacted)

docs.title: ach-cli token
docs.text:
Print the credential and nothing else. -o json prints {token, type, expires_at}
(type jwt or ek; expires_at is null for a key).

Usage:
  ach-cli token [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help             help for token
  -o, --output string    Output format: table|json (default "table")
      --profile string   Use this profile instead of the active one

docs.title: ach-cli upgrade
docs.text:
Download ach-cli from the GitHub releases page, check its sha256 against the
release's checksums.txt, and replace the running binary in place. Profiles in
~/.config/ach/config.yaml are untouched.

Without --version it installs the latest release. You must be able to write to
the binary's directory; for one under /usr/local/bin, run it with sudo.

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 failure (nothing replaced), 6 network error.

Usage:
  ach-cli upgrade [flags]

Examples:
  ach-cli upgrade
  ach-cli upgrade --version 1.1.8

Flags:
  -h, --help             help for upgrade
      --version string   install this release (e.g. 1.1.8) instead of the latest

docs.title: ach-cli whoami
docs.text:
Ask the Hub who the active credential belongs to and print:

  Profile  the profile used
  URL      the Hub
  User     your email
  Auth     session (OAuth login) or key ek-****abcd (--key / ACH_KEY / a key profile)
  Budget   spend / ceiling for your whole account
  Keys     keys held / keys allowed

Exit codes: 0 success, 3 not authorized, 6 network error.

Usage:
  ach-cli whoami [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help             help for whoami
      --key string       Authenticate with an environment key (ek-…)
  -o, --output string    Output format: table|json (default "table")
      --profile string   Use this profile instead of the active one
      --verbose          Dump request headers to stderr (credentials redacted)

docs.title: Helm values
docs.text:
The chart is oci://ghcr.io/ackstorm/charts/ach. This command prints every key with its default and is authoritative for the version you install:

helm show values oci://ghcr.io/ackstorm/charts/ach --version <X.Y.Z>

The sections follow the order of the chart's values.yaml. operator, platformApi, forwarder, gateway and contentService also take replicas, resources, args and initContainers; they are listed only where the default matters.

docs.title: installCRDs
docs.text: Key Default Purpose installCRDs true Install the CRDs with the release. helm upgrade upgrades them and helm uninstall keeps them. Set false when another tool applies the CRDs.

docs.title: enterprise
docs.text: Key Default Purpose enterprise.enabled false Turn on the Enterprise features: conversation classification, observability analytics and traces. Requires a signed agreement with ACKstorm. While false, the Enterprise values below render nothing.

docs.title: image
docs.text: Key Default Purpose image.repo ghcr.io/ackstorm/ach The one image every component runs. image.tag the chart's release Image tag. image.pullPolicy IfNotPresent Pull policy of every component. image.rebuildId "" Development only: a new value on each upgrade rolls every pod when the same tag was rebuilt.

docs.title: operator
docs.text:
Reconciles the ACH custom resources. In the default topology its Pod also runs content-service.

Key Default Purpose operator.enabled true Deploy the operator. operator.replicas 1 Replica count. operator.podLabels {} Extra labels on the operator Pod. operator.args operator, --metrics-bind-address=:8080, --metrics-secure=false Process arguments. Override them to serve metrics over TLS on :8443. operator.cache.size 10Gi Size of the artifact cache volume ach-operator-cache. operator.cache.accessMode ReadWriteOnce Access mode of the cache volume. ReadWriteMany is required with contentService.standalone. operator.cache.storageClassName "" Storage class of the cache volume; empty uses the cluster default. operator.initContainers [] Init containers of the operator Pod; they run before content-service too.

docs.title: platformApi
docs.text:
The REST API, the OAuth server and the console.

Key Default Purpose platformApi.enabled true Deploy platform-api. platformApi.admins.users [] Emails of the platform admins. Read at start, matched case-sensitively. platformApi.admins.sso [] Identity-provider groups whose members are admins. Re-read at login and at every token refresh. With both lists empty, every admin call answers 403. platformApi.headers x-ach-key, x-api-key, both resolve Request headers read for a credential, in order. Only mode: resolve is accepted. platformApi.userDefaults.maxBudget "" Spend ceiling in USD given to each user at first login. "" is no ceiling; 0 refuses every request. Changing it does not alter users who already have a ceiling. platformApi.userDefaults.budgetDuration "30d" Window after which the spend resets; "" never resets. platformApi.userDefaults.maxKeys 0 Environment keys one user may hold. 0 allows none until an admin grants an allowance. platformApi.keyExchange.tokenTTL 15m Lifetime of the token a ServiceAccount exchange returns, from 1m to 1h. platformApi.oauth.redirectHosts [] Hosts an OAuth client may redirect to over HTTPS. Loopback is always allowed. platformApi.teams.default [default] LiteLLM team aliases every user joins at login. A missing team fails the login. platformApi.teams.users {} Email → team aliases joined at login. platformApi.teams.sso {} Identity-provider group → team aliases joined at login. platformApi.console.chatUrl "" URL the console's Chat button opens; empty hides the button. platformApi.console.theme "" Default console skin: dark, light, pastel or red; empty follows the browser. platformApi.console.apps [] Tiles of the console's Apps page: name and url required; group, subtitle, icon, teams, admin optional. Empty hides the page. platformApi.observability.clickhouseUrl "" Enterprise. ClickHouse the observability routes read; empty leaves them answering 503. platformApi.observability.secretName "" Enterprise. Secret with ACH_OBSERVABILITY_CLICKHOUSE_USER and ACH_OBSERVABILITY_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD of a read-only user. Required with clickhouseUrl. platformApi.observability.projectIds [] Enterprise. Langfuse projects the routes may read. Required with clickhouseUrl. platformApi.observability.thanosUrl "" Enterprise. Prometheus query API for the gateway metrics.

docs.title: forwarder
docs.text:
The data path for model, MCP and A2A requests.

Key Default Purpose forwarder.enabled true Deploy the forwarder. forwarder.replicas 1 Replica count. forwarder.jwtSecretName ach-jwt-signing-keys Secret with the JWT signing keys. The operator creates it; it survives helm uninstall. forwarder.extraEnv [] Environment variables for the forwarder only. forwarder.headers x-ach-key, x-api-key, both resolve Request headers read for a credential, in order. resolve takes an ACH credential; passthrough forwards the backend's own key unchanged. forwarder.gemini.stripModelPrefixes [] Prefixes removed from the model name on the /gemini route; first match wins. forwarder.trustedIdP.issuer "" External OIDC issuer whose access tokens are accepted as Authorization: Bearer; empty turns it off. forwarder.trustedIdP.audiences [] Accepted aud values. Required with an issuer. forwarder.trustedIdP.claim email Token claim that names the ACH user.

docs.title: litellmConnection
docs.text:
The LiteLLM endpoint and master key, set once for every component.

Key Default Purpose litellmConnection.enabled true Configure the connection from these values. litellmConnection.endpoint http://litellm.litellm.svc.cluster.local:4000 LiteLLM base URL. litellmConnection.masterKeySecretRef.name litellm-master-key Secret with the LiteLLM master key. It must exist before the install. litellmConnection.masterKeySecretRef.key master_key Key inside that Secret. litellmConnection.masterKeySecretRef.namespace "" Namespace of the Secret; empty is the release namespace.

docs.title: security
docs.text:
Two Secrets that must exist before the install and must never change: replacing the encryption key makes stored LiteLLM keys unreadable, and replacing the pepper invalidates every issued credential.

Key Default Purpose security.keyEncryptionKey.secretRef.name ach-key-encryption-key Secret with the encryption key. security.keyEncryptionKey.secretRef.key dek Key inside it; the value is base64 of exactly 32 bytes. security.credentialHashPepper.secretRef.name ach-credential-hash-pepper Secret with the credential hash pepper. security.credentialHashPepper.secretRef.key pepper Key inside it.

docs.title: genai
docs.text:
What ACH tells GenAI clients (OpenCode) about itself.

Key Default Purpose genai.providerName ai-platform Provider id users sign in with. Lowercase letters, digits and -. Changing it signs every user out. genai.opencodePluginSpec a pinned git+https://github.com/ackstorm/opencode-oidc-provider.git tag Plugin OpenCode installs at sign-in; empty turns it off. genai.opencodeExtraProviders [] Other provider ids OpenCode may enable next to providerName. genai.defaultModel "" Default model for the client, when the user has access to it. genai.defaultSmallModel "" Default small model, under the same condition. genai.defaultEnvironment "" Environment the onboarding skill tells users to hydrate globally.

docs.title: gateway
docs.text:
The reverse proxy that puts platform-api, content-service and the forwarder behind one Service, ach-gateway. It serves ACH routes only: LiteLLM's own UI and API need their own host.

Key Default Purpose gateway.enabled true Deploy the gateway. false requires one Ingress per service. gateway.replicas 1 Replica count. gateway.extraEnv [] Environment variables for the gateway only.

docs.title: contentService
docs.text:
Serves plugin, skill, prompt and artifact archives.

Key Default Purpose contentService.enabled true Run content-service. contentService.standalone false false runs it inside the operator Pod. true runs its own Deployment and requires operator.cache.accessMode: ReadWriteMany. contentService.replicas 1 Replica count when standalone. contentService.initContainers [] Init containers of the standalone Deployment only.

docs.title: classifier
docs.text:
Enterprise. A job that labels idle sessions with one category.

Key Default Purpose classifier.enabled false Deploy the classifier. classifier.secretName "" Secret with the ClickHouse user, the model key and the Langfuse key pair. Required when enabled. classifier.clickhouseUrl "" ClickHouse the classifier reads sessions from. Required when enabled. classifier.projectId default Langfuse project to classify. classifier.modelUrl "" OpenAI-compatible base URL of the model. Required when enabled. classifier.model ackstorm.smart Model that classifies. classifier.langfuseUrl "" Langfuse the labels are written to; empty classifies and logs without writing. classifier.onlyUser "" Classify only this user's sessions. classifier.interval 10m Time between runs. classifier.idle 30m How long a session must be idle before it is classified. classifier.lookback 72h How far back sessions are considered. classifier.batch 50 Sessions per run. classifier.taxonomy {} Custom categories and rules; empty uses the built-in taxonomy. classifier.resources 50m CPU and 128Mi requested, 512Mi limit Resources of the classifier.

docs.title: migrate
docs.text: Key Default Purpose migrate.enabled true Run the schema migration Job before each install and upgrade.

docs.title: ingress
docs.text: Key Default Purpose ingress.enabled false Create the Ingress ach-public. ingress.className "" Ingress class; empty uses the cluster default. ingress.host "" Public hostname; empty matches any host. ingress.annotations {} Annotations on the Ingress. ingress.tls [] Copied to spec.tls. ingress.path / Path of the single rule. ingress.pathType Prefix Path type of the rule. ingress.service ach-gateway Backend Service. ingress.port 80 Backend port.

docs.title: metrics
docs.text:
The operator, platform-api, the forwarder and content-service serve /metrics without authentication; keep it inside the cluster. They carry prometheus.io/scrape annotations. The gateway serves no metrics.

Key Default Purpose metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled false Create a ServiceMonitor. Requires the Prometheus Operator CRDs, or the install fails. metrics.serviceMonitor.interval 30s Scrape interval. metrics.serviceMonitor.scrapeTimeout "" Scrape timeout; empty uses the Prometheus default. metrics.serviceMonitor.labels {} Labels your Prometheus selects ServiceMonitors by. metrics.prometheusRule.enabled false Create the recommended alert rules. Same CRD requirement. metrics.prometheusRule.labels {} Labels your Prometheus selects rules by. metrics.prometheusRule.includeP1Alerts true Include the two alerts on operator metrics. metrics.dashboards.enabled false Create one ConfigMap per Grafana dashboard for the Grafana sidecar. metrics.dashboards.namespace "" Namespace of those ConfigMaps; empty is the release namespace. The sidecar must watch it. metrics.dashboards.label grafana_dashboard Label the sidecar selects by. metrics.dashboards.labelValue "1" Value of that label. metrics.dashboards.folder ACH Grafana folder annotation. metrics.dashboards.labels {} Extra labels on the ConfigMaps.

docs.title: shutdown
docs.text:
How the gateway, the forwarder and platform-api stop on a rollout.

Key Default Purpose shutdown.drainSeconds 10 Wait before stopping, so the pod leaves its Service first. shutdown.timeoutSeconds 120 Time open requests get to finish. The pod grace period is the sum of both plus 5.

docs.title: extraEnv
docs.text:
Key Default Purpose extraEnv [] Environment variables added to the operator, platform-api, the forwarder, the gateway, content-service and the migration Job. The classifier gets none.

Settings with no value of their own are set here:

Variable Required Read by Value ACH_BASE_URL yes operator, platform-api, forwarder, content-service Public origin of the install. ACH_DB_URL yes operator, platform-api, forwarder, content-service, migration Job Postgres connection URL. ACH_REDIS_ADDR yes platform-api, forwarder, content-service host:port of Redis or Valkey. ACH_REDIS_PASSWORD, ACH_REDIS_TLS, ACH_REDIS_DB no same Redis password, TLS switch and database. ACH_DEX_ISSUER_URL, ACH_DEX_CLIENT_ID, ACH_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET yes platform-api The Dex client ACH signs users in with. ACH_OAUTH_ACCESS_TTL no platform-api Access token lifetime; default 1h, minimum 1m. ACH_OAUTH_REFRESH_TTL no platform-api Refresh token lifetime; default 720h, minimum 1h. ACH_DISABLE_UI_WRITES no platform-api true refuses Environments created from the console. ACH_PLUGIN_MAX_SIZE_MIB, ACH_SKILL_MAX_SIZE_MIB no operator Largest plugin and skill archive fetched; default 50. ACH_ORPHAN_CLEANUP_INTERVAL no operator Time between orphan-key cleanups; default 1h, minimum 5m. ACH_ORPHAN_CLEANUP_DRY_RUN no operator true logs the keys it would revoke and revokes none. ACH_ORPHAN_CLEANUP_MAX_REVOKE no operator A cleanup with more candidates than this revokes none; default 10.

docs.title: initContainers
docs.text: Key Default Purpose initContainers [] Init containers added to the operator, platform-api, forwarder, gateway and standalone content-service Deployments, before the component's own. The migration Job and the classifier get none.

docs.title: Forwarder JWT
docs.text: The forwarder mints this token on /mcp/<name> and /a2a/<name> when a BackendIdentityPolicy with spec.forwardIdentityJWT: true targets <name>. Every forwarded request gets a new token; there is no refresh.

docs.title: Header
docs.text: Field Value alg EdDSA (Ed25519) typ JWT kid Id of the signing key; resolve it against the JWKS

docs.title: Claims
docs.text:
Claim Value Present iss The forwarder's ACH_BASE_URL; HTTPS in production always sub Owner email of the calling key always email Same value as sub when the owner email is not empty groups Array of LiteLLM team aliases; see The groups claim when the set is not empty azp ek:<environment>; for audit, grants nothing on a token minted for an environment key aud mcp:<name> on /mcp/<name>, a2a:<name> on /a2a/<name> always iat Mint time, Unix seconds always exp iat + 120 always nbf — never jti — never

A verifier checks iss, aud and exp. It must not require nbf or jti.

docs.title: The groups claim
docs.text: Calling key groups pk_ The caller's LiteLLM teams ∩ authorizedTeams of the active Environments whose runtime.mcpServers (or runtime.a2aAgents) contains <name> ek_ The same set, computed for the key's owner email; never the Environment's full authorizedTeams Property Value Element LiteLLM team_alias, or team_id when the alias is empty. An authorizedTeams entry written as a team id appears as that id Order Sorted, deduplicated Renaming a LiteLLM team Changes the value in the claim Excluded ACH's internal teams ach-env-* and ach-user-* Empty set The claim is omitted Revocation None: a backend trusts the claim until exp A user removed from a LiteLLM team keeps the group, on pk_ and ek_, for at most 180 s (exp 120 s + 60 s membership cache) A team removed from Environment.spec.authorizedTeams stays in the claim for at most about 7 min (exp 120 s + 5 min refresh)

docs.title: JWKS endpoint
docs.text:
GET <iss>/.well-known/jwks.json
Response header Value Content-Type application/jwk-set+json Cache-Control public, max-age=3600 JWK field Value kty OKP crv Ed25519 use sig alg EdDSA kid Id of the key; matches the token header x The 32-byte public key, base64url without padding

keys holds one key, or two during a rotation: both stay published for at least 24 hours before the old one is removed (JWT key rotation).

Implementation: internal/forwarder/jwt/signer.go.

docs.title: Your first Environment
docs.text:
In this tutorial you install ach-cli, sign in to your organisation's ACH, put an Environment into a folder and start Claude Code on it. It takes about ten minutes.

You need:

  • The URL of your ACH, for example https://ach.example.com. Your platform team has it.
  • An Environment your team may use. The examples call it quickstart; use a name from your own list in step 3.
  • Linux or macOS, with Claude Code installed.

On Windows, or with another tool, follow the same steps with Install or update ach-cli and Find, install and update Environments.

docs.title: 1. Install ach-cli
docs.text:
VERSION=$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/ackstorm/ach/releases/latest | sed -n 's/.*"tag_name": *"v\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
OS=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
ARCH=$(uname -m); case "$ARCH" in x86_64) ARCH=amd64;; aarch64) ARCH=arm64;; esac
FILE="ach-cli_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz"
curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/ackstorm/ach/releases/download/v${VERSION}/${FILE}"
curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/ackstorm/ach/releases/download/v${VERSION}/checksums.txt"
grep " ${FILE}\$" checksums.txt | if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null; then sha256sum -c -; else shasum -a 256 -c -; fi
tar -xzf "$FILE" ach-cli
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && mv ach-cli ~/.local/bin/

The checksum line prints OK. Check the install:

ach-cli --version

If the shell does not find ach-cli, add ~/.local/bin to your PATH.

docs.title: 2. Sign in
docs.text:
ach-cli login https://ach.example.com

Press Enter to accept the profile name default, then choose 1 to open the browser on this machine. Sign in with your organisation account. The terminal continues when the browser says you are signed in.

ach-cli whoami

whoami prints your email after User and session after Auth.

docs.title: 3. Look at your Environments
docs.text:
ach-cli environment list

The list holds the Environments your teams may use. Pick one, then look at what it contains:

ach-cli environment describe quickstart

describe prints the Environment's runtime (models, MCP servers, A2A agents) and its context (plugins, skills, prompts, artifacts).

docs.title: 4. Put it in a folder
docs.text:
mkdir -p ~/Projects && cd ~/Projects
ach-cli environment clone quickstart --target claude-code

clone creates ~/Projects/quickstart and hydrates the Environment into it: it writes the Environment's plugins and skills under .claude/, its MCP servers into .mcp.json, and a record of what it wrote under .ach/. It lists what it added, each line starting with +, and ends with Finished.

docs.title: 5. Start Claude Code on it
docs.text:
cd ~/Projects/quickstart
ach-cli launch claude

launch starts Claude Code in the folder clone just filled; add --update-environments on a later day to bring the folder up to date with the Environment first. Inside Claude Code, type / to see the commands the Environment's plugins added, and /mcp to see its MCP servers. Leave Claude Code to return to the shell.

Any project you create under ~/Projects/quickstart gets the same Environment.

docs.title: 6. Check and update
docs.text:
ach-cli environment status

status lists what is installed in this folder and ends with up to date. When your platform team changes the Environment, status shows what changed, and this brings the folder up to date:

ach-cli environment hydrate

docs.title: 7. Remove it
docs.text:
ach-cli environment uninstall quickstart

uninstall removes what hydrate wrote and leaves your own files. The folder stays; delete it if you no longer want it.

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• Sign in to an MCP server the Environment brought.
  • Find, install and update Environments: a global install, several tools, one plugin only.
  • Create and manage environment keys for an agent or a CI job.
  • Concepts explains Environments, teams and keys.

docs.title: Install or update ach-cli
docs.text:
ach-cli is one binary with no dependencies. Each release carries one archive per platform and a checksums.txt:

Platform Archive Linux, macOS (amd64, arm64) ach-cli_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz Windows (amd64) ach-cli_<version>_windows_amd64.zip

<version> is the release tag without its leading v; <os> is linux or darwin.

You need curl and tar on Linux and macOS, or PowerShell on Windows.

docs.title: Linux and macOS
docs.text:
VERSION=$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/ackstorm/ach/releases/latest | sed -n 's/.*"tag_name": *"v\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
OS=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
ARCH=$(uname -m); case "$ARCH" in x86_64) ARCH=amd64;; aarch64) ARCH=arm64;; esac
FILE="ach-cli_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz"
curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/ackstorm/ach/releases/download/v${VERSION}/${FILE}"
curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/ackstorm/ach/releases/download/v${VERSION}/checksums.txt"
grep " ${FILE}\$" checksums.txt | if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null; then sha256sum -c -; else shasum -a 256 -c -; fi
tar -xzf "$FILE" ach-cli
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && mv ach-cli ~/.local/bin/

The checksum line must print OK. If it does not, stop: the download is corrupt or is not the published file.

~/.local/bin must be on your PATH.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
In PowerShell. The build is amd64; it also runs on ARM Windows.

$v = (Invoke-RestMethod https://api.github.com/repos/ackstorm/ach/releases/latest).tag_name.TrimStart('v')
Invoke-WebRequest "https://github.com/ackstorm/ach/releases/download/v$v/ach-cli_${v}_windows_amd64.zip" -OutFile ach-cli.zip
Expand-Archive ach-cli.zip -DestinationPath "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\ach-cli" -Force
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('Path', [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','User') + ";$env:LOCALAPPDATA\ach-cli", 'User')

Open a new terminal so the PATH change applies.

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
ach-cli upgrade                    # the latest release
ach-cli upgrade --version 1.1.8    # a given release

upgrade downloads the release for your platform, checks it against checksums.txt and replaces the running binary. Your profiles in ~/.config/ach/config.yaml are not touched.

Message Do permission denied You cannot write to the binary's directory. Run it with sudo, or install under ~/.local/bin unknown command "upgrade" This ach-cli predates the command. Run the install commands above again

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
ach-cli --version

It prints the version you installed. Next: sign in.

docs.title: Install the ACH agent plugins
docs.text:
ACH publishes three plugins that teach an AI coding agent to work with it. They live in a plugin marketplace named ach, at the root of the ACH repository.

Plugin For The agent learns to ach-cli Every user Sign in, find and hydrate Environments, sign in to MCP servers, manage ek- keys, use ach-cli local ach-gitops Platform admins Write Environments, marketplaces, Plugins, Skills and the other ACH custom resources ach-install Operators Install, configure and upgrade the Helm chart

None of them contains the URL of your ACH: ach-cli reads it from your profile, or from ACH_URL before you first sign in.

You need the agent tool installed. The Environment route also needs ach-cli and a sign-in.

docs.title: Through an Environment
docs.text:
If your platform team serves the plugins through an Environment, hydrating it installs them, for every tool ACH supports:

ach-cli environment search ach-cli           # which Environment has it
ach-cli environment hydrate <environment> --target <tool>

docs.title: Directly in Claude Code
docs.text:
claude plugin marketplace add ackstorm/ach
claude plugin install ach-cli@ach

docs.title: Directly in Codex
docs.text:
codex plugin marketplace add ackstorm/ach
codex plugin add ach-cli@ach

docs.title: Verify
docs.text: Start the tool and ask it to list your ACH Environments. It runs ach-cli environment list.

docs.title: For platform admins: serve them through ACH
docs.text:
Register the repository as a PluginMarketplace and list the plugins in an Environment; users then get them with ach-cli environment hydrate:

apiVersion: ach.ackstorm.ai/v1alpha1
kind: PluginMarketplace
metadata:
  name: ach
spec:
  type: github
  github:
    repo: ackstorm/ach
    ref: main
  refresh:
    interval: 1h
    maxStaleness: 24h
---
apiVersion: ach.ackstorm.ai/v1alpha1
kind: Environment
metadata:
  name: baseline
spec:
  context:
    plugins:
      - ach-cli@ach
  authorizedTeams:
    - default

Put ach-cli@ach in the Environment named by the chart value genai.defaultEnvironment: OpenCode users get a short bootstrap skill (<provider>-ach) from /clients/opencode/config that installs ach-cli, signs in and hydrates that Environment, and from there the ach-cli plugin takes over. Keep ach-gitops and ach-install in the Environments of the people who run the platform.

docs.title: Install a plugin or skill from a git repository
docs.text:
ach-cli local installs a plugin or a skill straight from a git repository into a tool. It uses no Environment and no sign-in, so nothing it installs is governed, audited or shared with your team. Use it to try something. For anything a team relies on, ask a platform admin to publish it in an Environment and hydrate that.

You need ach-cli and git 2.31 or later on your PATH.

docs.title: Register the repository
docs.text:
ach-cli local repo add github:owner/repo --name <repo>
ach-cli local repo add git:https://git.example.com/group/repo.git#main --name <repo>
ach-cli local repo list
Part Meaning github:owner/repo[#ref] A GitHub repository git:https://host/path[.git][#ref] Any other git host #ref Branch, tag or commit; main when left out --name Required. The name you use for the repository afterwards --path <dir> For a skills repository: the folder that holds the <skill>/SKILL.md directories

Local paths are not supported.

For a private repository pass --token, or set GITHUB_TOKEN (for github:) or GITLAB_TOKEN (for git:). Some GitLab setups need --auth basic-oauth2.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
ach-cli local plugin install <plugin>@<repo> --target claude-code
ach-cli local skill install <skill>@<repo> --target codex,opencode

--target is one or more of claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, opencode and pi. The install goes into the current folder; -g puts it in the tool's global configuration. --dry-run prints the plan and writes nothing.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
ach-cli local plugin list     # or: ach-cli local skill list

The item is listed, and the tool shows it the next time it starts.

docs.title: Update and remove
docs.text:
ach-cli local plugin outdated                 # compare with the source; changes nothing
ach-cli local plugin update                   # all, or <plugin>@<repo>
ach-cli local plugin uninstall <plugin>@<repo>
ach-cli local repo remove <repo>

ach-cli local skill has the same commands.

docs.text: • ach-cli local in the command reference.
