docs.text: Writing ACH's custom resources (Environment, Plugin, PluginMarketplace, Skill, SkillMarketplace, Prompt, Artifact, BackendIdentityPolicy) is covered by the ach-gitops agent skill (plugins/ach-gitops/skills/ach-gitops/); field-by-field detail is in the API reference.

docs.title: Choosing a key: pk_ vs ek_
docs.text:
• pk_ (Personal Key) — dev / personal use. Authorizes against the UNION of your capabilities; NOT bound to any Environment (no access-group scoping, no Environment attribution tag). Convenient for local experimentation.
  • ek_ (Environment Key) — agents / CI / workloads. Environment-scoped: capability-gated to one Environment and carries its attribution tag. Use this for anything reproducible or governed.

A recommended Prometheus alert: watch ach_forwarder_requests_total{key_type="pk"} on runtime routes to catch pk_ used where an ek_ belongs. There is no server-side pk_-forbid toggle (honoring the frozen permanent decision); enforcement, if wanted, is the deployer's LiteLLM choice.

docs.title: ek_ lifecycle: expiry, suspend, resume, revoke
docs.text:
An ek_ can optionally be created with an expiration time, and can be manually suspended and resumed without losing the credential. From the CLI (a key is named by the name it was saved under, or by its ekid_…):

ach-cli keys create <env> --name ci-bot --expires 90d
ach-cli keys suspend ci-bot      # ach-cli keys resume ci-bot undoes it
ach-cli keys revoke ci-bot

The routes behind them, also usable directly or through the web console:

  • POST /platform/keys accepts an optional expires_at (RFC3339, must be in the future — a past or malformed value is 400 invalid_argument). Omitting it keeps the existing perpetual behavior. Expiry is enforced by ACH only: no LiteLLM-side duration is ever set, and it is not editable after create — create a new credential instead.
  • POST /platform/keys/{key_id}/suspend and POST /platform/keys/{key_id}/resume disable and re-enable an ek_ in place. Both are idempotent when the key is already in the requested state. Resume fails 409 on a revoked or expired key, and 403 unauthorized_team if you no longer hold the Environment's access. The backing credential is never deleted or re-minted — the same ek_ keeps working once resumed.
  • DELETE /platform/keys/{key_id} revokes from any state and is idempotent; it cannot be undone.

Suspension may take up to 60 seconds to apply. Requests already in progress may continue.

docs.title: Spend ceilings
docs.text:
Every ACH credential can carry a spend ceiling. They are enforced by LiteLLM on three independent counters, and a request is refused as soon as ANY of them is over budget — there is no hierarchy, whichever is crossed first wins:

Ceiling Covers Set by Your own your pk_ and every ek_ you own, in every Environment the deployer, as a default seeded at your first login; an admin, per person (below) Environment the pooled spend of every ek_ issued for one Environment, across all owners an admin, via Environment.spec.budget in the CR Per key one ek_ on its own you, when you create the key or at any time after

Set a ceiling when you create a key:

curl -X POST https://<ach>/platform/keys \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACH_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"environment":"demo","name":"ci","budget":{"max_budget":25,"budget_duration":"30d"}}'

…or change it later (the key keeps working; only the ceiling moves):

curl -X PATCH https://<ach>/platform/keys/<key_id>/budget \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACH_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"max_budget":50}'

max_budget is in LiteLLM's spend unit (USD) and must be >= 0; 0 is a real ceiling that refuses everything once any spend lands. budget_duration (e.g. "30d") is the reset window — omit it for a budget that never resets. Only the key's owner may change its budget.

An admin can retune one person's own ceiling — the one covering their pk_ and every ek_ they own — with the same body:

curl -X PATCH https://<ach>/platform/admin/users/someone%40example.com/budget \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACH_ADMIN_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"max_budget":200,"budget_duration":"30d"}'

The email is a path segment (URL-encode the @ if your client needs it) and need not have logged in yet — the ceiling is waiting when they do. The value is durable: the deployment-wide default is seeded only onto a tag that has no ceiling yet, so logging in never overwrites it. The flip side is that raising the deployment-wide default does not retune anyone who already has one — this route is how you do that.

When a ceiling is reached, the request fails with HTTP 422 and a body naming the counter that blocked. Retrying does not help until the ceiling is raised or the budget resets:

{"error":{"message":"Budget has been exceeded! Tag=key:ekid_… Current cost: 25.4, Max budget: 25.0","type":"budget_exceeded","param":null,"code":"422"}}

An MCP tool call carries the same text as {"detail":"Budget has been exceeded! …"}.

Tag=user:… means your own ceiling, Tag=environment:… the Environment's pooled one, and Tag=key:… that single key's. Raise the named ceiling (or wait for its reset window) and traffic resumes within about ten seconds. Two caveats: the comparison is post-paid, so the request that crosses the line is served and the NEXT one is refused; and revoking a key deletes its ceiling along with it.

GET /platform/keys reports one of five effective states, in priority order when more than one applies:

State Meaning Recovery revoked Permanently withdrawn. Cannot be recovered; create a new credential. expired Its expires_at has passed. Create a new credential; expiry is not editable. suspended Manually disabled by the owner. POST .../resume, subject to current access and validity. invalid Owner no longer has access to the Environment. Automatically usable again once access returns — no action needed. active Enabled, unexpired, not revoked, owner has access. None required.

?status= filters on this effective state; an unrecognized value is 400 invalid_argument. Because the filter is applied AFTER the effective state is derived (an invalid row is still persisted active), a filtered page can hold fewer than limit items even while next_cursor is non-empty — keep paging until next_cursor is empty rather than stopping at a short page.

Release notes: once any ek_ has been suspended or given an expiry, the database cannot be rolled back below this release (D-29) — see references/troubleshooting.md for the exact refusal text and recovery.

docs.title: Start a tool on an Environment
docs.text:
ach-cli launch starts one tool, hydrating an Environment for it first when you ask, so the tool opens on the current version of the Environment.

You need to be signed in, and the tool must be installed and on your PATH.

launch name Tool claude Claude Code codex Codex gemini Gemini CLI opencode OpenCode pi pi

docs.title: Start the tool
docs.text:
cd ~/Projects/my-project
ach-cli launch claude --environment <environment>

launch hydrates <environment> into the current folder for Claude Code, starts claude there, and exits with the tool's exit code. ACH_ENVIRONMENT is the same as --environment.

docs.title: Start it on what the folder already has
docs.text:
cd ~/Projects/<environment>
ach-cli launch opencode                          # as the folder is
ach-cli launch opencode --update-environments    # update its Environments first

Without --environment, launch starts the tool without hydrating. --update-environments (or --update-envs) first updates every Environment already hydrated in that folder. An Environment installed globally with -g does not count.

docs.title: Start it in another folder
docs.text: ach-cli launch codex --environment <environment> --dir ~/work/infra

docs.title: Pass arguments to the tool
docs.text:
Put the tool's own flags after --:

ach-cli launch codex --environment <environment> -- --model <model>

docs.title: Nothing starts
docs.text:
launch does not start the tool when:

  • the tool is not on your PATH;
  • there is no Environment to hydrate: none named and none in the folder;
  • the hydrate fails. The message and exit code are those of environment hydrate.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Inside the tool, the Environment's skills, plugins and MCP servers are listed. From a second terminal in the same folder:

ach-cli environment status

It shows the Environment, the tool as its target, and up to date.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• ach-cli launch in the command reference: launch takes the flags of environment hydrate except --target, --only, --dry-run and --allow-symlinks.
  • Find, install and update Environments.

docs.title: Create and manage environment keys
docs.text:
An environment key (ek-…) lets something that cannot sign in with a browser use ACH: an agent runtime, a CI job, a script. A key works for one Environment, is long-lived and is a secret.

You need to be signed in and have access to the Environment.

docs.title: Create a key
docs.text:
ach-cli keys create <environment> --name ci-deploy

The key is printed once and stored nowhere else. Put it straight into the secret store of whatever uses it.

Flag Effect --name Required. What the key is for; every other command takes this name --expires 90d The key expires after that time. Also takes a duration (720h) or a date (2026-12-31T00:00:00Z). Cannot be changed later --max-budget 20 The key may spend at most that many USD --budget-duration 30d The budget resets after that period. Needs --max-budget -o json Prints {name, id, environment, key, expires_at}

Your own budget still applies on top of a key's budget.

docs.title: Use a key
docs.text:
Send it in the x-ach-key header (x-api-key works too):

For URL Models, OpenAI-compatible https://ach.example.com/v1 An MCP server of the Environment https://ach.example.com/mcp/<server> 
curl -H "x-ach-key: $ACH_KEY" https://ach.example.com/v1/models

/v1/models lists chat models; add ?types=embedding or ?types=all for the others.

To run ach-cli with a key, pass --key ek-…, set ACH_KEY, or save it in a profile.

docs.title: List your keys
docs.text:
ach-cli keys list                          # active keys
ach-cli keys list --status all
ach-cli keys list --environment <environment>
State Meaning To use it again active Works suspended You paused it ach-cli keys resume expired Its expiry passed Create a new key invalid You lost access to its Environment, or your organisation's single sign-on no longer accepts you It works again when access returns; in the second case, after you run ach-cli login revoked Withdrawn for good Create a new key

docs.title: Suspend, resume, revoke
docs.text:
ach-cli keys suspend ci-deploy
ach-cli keys resume ci-deploy
ach-cli keys revoke ci-deploy      # asks first; --yes skips the question

Each takes the key's name or its ekid_… id. A suspension applies within 60 seconds. A revoked key cannot be restored.

docs.title: Change a key's budget
docs.text:
ach-cli keys budget ci-deploy --max-budget 50 --budget-duration 30d

The new budget applies after about 10 seconds. The key keeps working.

docs.title: The key limit
docs.text: You may hold a limited number of keys that are not revoked. ach-cli whoami shows held and allowed after Keys. At the limit, keys create fails with 403 key_limit_reached: revoke a key, or ask a platform admin to raise your limit.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
ach-cli keys list
curl -H "x-ach-key: $ACH_KEY" https://ach.example.com/v1/models

The key is listed as active, and the request returns the Environment's models.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• ach-cli keys in the command reference.
  • Keys and budgets explains how the budgets of a user, an Environment and a key combine.

docs.title: Use ACH models from Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode
docs.text:
By default a tool keeps its own model login, and ACH only gives it MCP servers, plugins and skills. This page sends the tool's model requests through ACH as well, so they use your ACH sign-in and count against your ACH budget.

You need to be signed in with ach-cli login, not with an environment key, and ach-cli must be on your PATH: the tools start it without your shell, so an alias is not enough.

docs.title: Claude Code on your Claude subscription
docs.text:
ach-cli launch claude                       # add --environment <env> to hydrate first
alias claude='ach-cli launch claude --'     # every claude goes through ACH

launch claude keeps your Claude login, so your subscription pays Anthropic, and still sends the model traffic through ACH. While claude runs, ach-cli serves your ACH URL on a local port, adds your ACH sign-in to every request (renewed before it expires) and passes the rest, your Claude login included, untouched. --profile picks the profile; --key ek-… sends that key instead, so spend also counts on the key and its Environment.

You set nothing yourself. ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS in your shell are ignored with a warning. A Claude settings file whose env sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL would send claude past ACH, so launch stops and names the file. If your ACH session ends while claude runs, claude shows API Error: 401 …: run ach-cli login in another terminal and the next message works without restarting claude. /remote-control stays unavailable: Claude Code turns it off behind any gateway.

docs.title: Claude Code and Codex
docs.text:
Add --models when you hydrate:

ach-cli environment hydrate <environment> --target claude-code --models
ach-cli environment hydrate <environment> --target codex --models

environment clone and launch take --models too, except launch claude, which routes claude through ACH on its own (see above).

Pass --models every time you hydrate or launch in that folder. A run without it removes what --models wrote, which is also how you go back to the tool's own login.

docs.title: What --models writes
docs.text:
The tool gets your ACH as its model endpoint and ach-cli token as the command that supplies the credential.

Claude Code, .claude/settings.json:

{
  "apiKeyHelper": "ach-cli token",
  "env": { "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://ach.example.com" }
}

Codex, .codex/config.toml:

model_provider = "ach"

[model_providers.ach]
name = "ACH"
base_url = "https://ach.example.com/v1"
wire_api = "responses"

[model_providers.ach.auth]
command = "ach-cli token"
refresh_interval_ms = 300000

docs.title: ach-cli token
docs.text:
ach-cli token prints the access token of the active profile on one line and nothing else. It renews the token when it is close to expiry. ach-cli token -o json adds the token's type and expiry.

Any other tool that takes a command for its credential can use it the same way, with https://ach.example.com/v1 as an OpenAI-compatible base URL.

docs.title: OpenCode
docs.text:
OpenCode signs in to ACH with its own plugin and needs neither --models nor ach-cli:

opencode auth login https://ach.example.com   # installs the ACH sign-in plugin
opencode auth login <provider>                # signs you in
opencode service restart                      # OpenCode v2: plugins load when the service starts

<provider> is the name your platform team chose for ACH; they have it. On OpenCode v1 the second command is opencode auth login -p <provider>.

After the restart, the models of <provider> come from ACH.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Start the tool and send a prompt. Then:

ach-cli whoami

The spend after Budget grows with your requests.

docs.title: What you can reach
docs.text: The models you get are those of the Environments your teams may use, as listed by ach-cli environment describe <environment>.

docs.text:

  • Create and manage environment keys for an agent or a CI job, which cannot sign in with a browser.

docs.title: Sign in to an MCP server
docs.text:
Hydrating an Environment writes its MCP servers into your tool's configuration. Each entry points at https://ach.example.com/mcp/<server>. An A2A agent of the Environment appears as an MCP server named a2a-<agent>.

When you hydrate with your sign-in, the entries hold no credential: the tool signs in to ACH itself, once per server, with your single sign-on. A hydrate with an environment key writes that key into the entries, and there is nothing to sign in to.

You need an Environment hydrated into the tool.

docs.title: Sign in
docs.text:
List the servers first. A server in the list is configured, even when the tool says it needs authentication: sign in to it, do not add it again.

Tool List Sign in Claude Code claude mcp list claude mcp login <server>, or /mcp inside a session Codex codex mcp list codex mcp login <server> OpenCode opencode mcp list opencode mcp auth <server>

The command opens a browser on the ACH sign-in page. For some servers the browser makes one more stop, at the consent screen of the service behind the server (for example a Google or GitHub account); approve it there.

Finish the sign-in in the browser that opened it. A link copied into another browser or browser profile is refused.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text: List again. The server shows as connected, and its tools appear in the tool.

docs.title: Sign in over SSH
docs.text:
The tool waits for the browser on the remote machine's localhost, so the last redirect fails in your local browser with "127.0.0.1 refused to connect". Either:

  • forward the callback port before you sign in: ssh -L <port>:localhost:<port> <host>; or
  • copy the whole failed address from the browser bar and open it on the remote machine: curl -s -o /dev/null "<address>". Only do this for an address that starts with http://127.0.0.1: or http://localhost:.

Then list the servers in the tool to check.

docs.title: The tool does not show a server
docs.text:
1. Hydrate again and list again:

    ach-cli environment hydrate

  2. Check that one of your Environments provides it:

    ach-cli environment describe <environment>
ach-cli environment search <server>

If none does, the server is not available to you. A platform admin adds it to an Environment.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Symptom Cause Do 401 on every request The tool never signed in to that server Run the tool's sign-in command 401 after signing in The stored sign-in is no longer valid Sign out of that server in the tool, then sign in again 403 Your teams have no access to that server Signing in again does not help. A platform admin grants it through an Environment Connected, but no tools The service behind the server has no consent from you Run the tool's sign-in command again and approve the consent screen. If it stays empty, ask a platform admin "this browser did not start the authorization request" The sign-in finished in another browser than the one that started it, or cookies are blocked for your ACH Start the sign-in again from the tool A server disappeared The Environment changed Hydrate again

docs.title: Leave the entries as hydrate wrote them
docs.text: Do not add a header, a key or an OAuth setting to an MCP entry that hydrate wrote. A credential header turns off the tool's own sign-in, and the next hydrate rewrites the entry.

docs.title: Sign in to ACH
docs.text:
You sign in once per machine, through your organisation's single sign-on. ach-cli keeps the session in a profile and renews it by itself.

You need ach-cli installed and the URL of your ACH, for example https://ach.example.com. Your platform team has it.

docs.title: Sign in
docs.text:
ach-cli login https://ach.example.com

login asks for a profile name (accept default), then how to finish:

  1. The browser on this machine. It opens the sign-in page; when you are done the terminal continues by itself.
  2. Another device. It prints a URL and a code. Open the URL in a browser on any device, check that the code matches, and sign in.

Without the URL argument, login takes it from ACH_URL, or asks.

To sign in again later, name the profile:

ach-cli login https://ach.example.com --profile default

docs.title: Sign in from a machine without a browser
docs.text:
Over SSH or in a container, skip the menu:

ach-cli login https://ach.example.com --no-browser

It prints the URL and the code for another device, and waits.

docs.title: Check who you are
docs.text:
ach-cli whoami
Line Shows Profile The profile used URL Your ACH User Your email Auth session after login, or a masked key Budget Your spend and your ceiling Keys Environment keys you hold, and how many you may hold

whoami -o json prints the same as JSON.

docs.title: Pick up a new group
docs.text:
When someone adds you to a single sign-on group, run:

ach-cli refresh

It joins the teams your groups map to, without a browser. The Environments of those teams appear in ach-cli environment list a few minutes later. refresh only adds teams.

docs.title: Use more than one profile
docs.text:
A profile is a URL plus a credential, stored in ~/.config/ach/config.yaml. One is enough unless you work with several ACH installs.

ach-cli login https://ach.example.com --profile prod   # a second profile
ach-cli profile list                                   # * marks the default
ach-cli profile show prod
ach-cli profile use prod                               # make it the default
ach-cli profile rename prod production
ach-cli profile remove production                      # --force for the default one

To use another profile for one command, pass --profile <name> or set ACH_PROFILE.

docs.title: Sign out
docs.text:
ach-cli logout

The session is removed from the profile; the URL stays. Environment keys you created keep working until you revoke them.

docs.title: Set up a machine that never has a browser
docs.text:
A CI runner or an agent host signs in with an environment key instead of a session. Create the key on a machine where you are signed in, then on the target machine either save it in a profile:

ach-cli profile add ci --url https://ach.example.com --key ek-…

or set two variables and keep no file at all:

export ACH_URL=https://ach.example.com
export ACH_KEY=ek-…

With both variables set, login, logout, profile and token exit 1: there is no profile.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• ach-cli login, profile, whoami in the command reference.
  • Troubleshoot ach-cli when a command says you are not signed in.

docs.title: Troubleshoot ach-cli
docs.text:
Start with these two; both only read:

ach-cli whoami               # profile, URL, user, budget
ach-cli environment status   # what is installed in this folder

Every failure prints error: and the reason, often followed by a hint: with the command to run. Add --verbose to a network command to print the request line and its headers, with credentials redacted.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning Do 0 Success 1 Any other error: wrong usage, a missing or malformed credential, a server that cannot be reached, a refused request Read the message 2 Hydrate would overwrite a file you edited See A file you edited blocks hydrate 3 Not authorized: the sign-in or key was rejected, or you have no access to that Environment or admin command Sign in again; if that does not help, a platform admin grants the access 4 The record under .ach/ names another Environment than the one you asked for Hydrate the Environment the folder holds, or pass --force 5 The record under .ach/, or the server's answer, has a format this ach-cli does not know Run ach-cli upgrade. --force rewrites the local record 6 The server answered that it is unavailable; for whoami, refresh and upgrade, also a server that cannot be reached Retry 8 ~/.config/ach/config.yaml, or a record under .ach/, cannot be read or written Check the file and its permissions

launch exits with the tool's own code once the tool has started.

An ek- key used on another Environment than its own fails with wrong_environment and exit 1.

docs.title: Not signed in, or a command returns 401
docs.text:
Sign in again, naming your profile:

ach-cli login https://ach.example.com --profile default

A session ends when your organisation's single sign-on stops accepting it.

docs.title: An Environment is missing from the list
docs.text: You do not have access to it; a platform admin grants it by adding one of your teams to the Environment. If you were just added to a single sign-on group, run ach-cli refresh and wait a few minutes.

docs.title: ach-cli X is older than the server (Y)
docs.text: Run ach-cli upgrade. Commands usually keep working until you do. An unknown field error from hydrate has the same cause.

docs.title: another ach-cli is running on this workspace
docs.text: A hydrate is still running in that folder. Wait for it, or pass --lock-timeout 2m to wait up to that long.

docs.title: refusing to hydrate, or path leaves the workspace
docs.text: A path in the folder is a symbolic link that leads outside it, for example a .claude or .mcp.json linked to another directory. Remove the link or point it inside the folder. Links that stay inside the folder are accepted, and a global install (-g) is exempt. environment uninstall and ach-cli local apply the same rule.

docs.title: no agent target detected
docs.text: The folder has no tool configuration yet, or has several. Pass --target <tool>.

docs.title: nothing hydrated in this folder yet
docs.text: environment hydrate or launch --update-environments ran without an Environment name in a folder that holds none. Name one, or create the folder with ach-cli environment clone <environment>.

docs.title: Two plugins write the same file
docs.text: By default each file is installed under its plugin's name, so both stay. --conflict skip and --conflict overwrite keep one of them; --conflict refuse stops with an error.

docs.title: A file you edited blocks hydrate
docs.text: Hydrate names the file and exits 2. When you update a whole folder with no Environment name, it reports the failure per Environment and exits 1. Keep your edit and leave it, or pass --force to replace the file with the Environment's version. ach-cli environment status lists the files you edited.

docs.title: Budget exceeded
docs.text:
A model request fails with HTTP 422 and a message that names the budget that was reached:

In the message Budget Who raises it Tag=user:… Your own, across everything you use A platform admin Tag=environment:… The Environment's, shared by all its keys A platform admin Tag=key:… One key's You: ach-cli keys budget

ach-cli whoami shows your own spend and ceiling. Retrying does not help until the budget is raised or its period resets.

docs.title: Find, install and update Environments
docs.text:
An Environment is a named set your platform team publishes: models, MCP servers and A2A agents, plus plugins, skills, prompts and artifacts. Installing one into an agent tool is called hydrating.

You need to be signed in. <tool> below is one of claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, opencode or pi.

docs.title: Find an Environment
docs.text:
ach-cli environment list                    # the Environments your teams may use
ach-cli environment describe <environment>  # what one contains
ach-cli environment search <text>           # which Environment has a plugin, skill, MCP server…

search matches the name and description of each Environment and the name of everything it serves, ignoring case. Several words must all match. It does not search inside a skill or a plugin.

All three take -o json.

docs.title: Install one for every project
docs.text:
ach-cli environment hydrate <environment> -g --target <tool>

-g writes into the tool's own global configuration, so every project on the machine gets the Environment. This suits an organisation-wide baseline.

docs.title: Install one into a folder
docs.text:
cd ~/Projects
ach-cli environment clone <environment> --target <tool>

clone creates ./<environment>, hydrates into it, and removes the folder again if that fails. It refuses a folder that exists and is not empty. A second argument names another folder.

Everything under that folder gets the Environment, because Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode read the configuration of each parent folder:

~/Projects/
  <environment>/      one folder per Environment
    <project>/        your work; a git repository or not

To hydrate into the folder you are in instead:

ach-cli environment hydrate <environment> --target <tool>

--target takes several tools (--target claude-code,opencode). Inside a folder that already holds one tool's configuration you may leave it out.

Hydrate adds the folders it writes (.ach/, .claude/, …) to a .gitignore in that folder.

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
cd ~/Projects/<environment>
ach-cli environment hydrate                       # every Environment recorded here
ach-cli environment hydrate <environment> --sync      # also remove what the Environment dropped
ach-cli environment hydrate <environment> --dry-run   # show the changes, write nothing

Hydrate lists what it changed, one line per item: + added, ~ changed, - removed. After eight lines it prints a count; --verbose shows them all.

Hydrate does not overwrite a file you edited: it stops, names the file and exits 2. Keep your edit, or pass --force to take the Environment's version. environment status marks such files with ! edited.

Do not edit the tool's configuration while hydrate runs: hydrate reads the file, merges its entries and writes it back, so a save in between is lost.

docs.title: Install one plugin or skill
docs.text:
ach-cli environment hydrate <environment> --only plugin/<name>   # or skill/<name>

It adds that item to what is already installed and writes no MCP configuration.

docs.title: See what is installed
docs.text:
ach-cli environment status                    # this folder
ach-cli environment status <environment> -g   # the global install
ach-cli environment status --files            # every file hydrate wrote
ach-cli environment status --offline          # without asking the server

status lists what is installed and the files you edited, then asks the server whether each Environment changed since you hydrated it: up to date, or + added, - removed, ~ new content. It downloads nothing.

docs.title: Remove
docs.text:
ach-cli environment uninstall <environment> --dry-run   # show what would go
ach-cli environment uninstall <environment>             # this folder; -g for the global install

Only what hydrate wrote is removed. In files it shares with you (.mcp.json, .codex/config.toml, .opencode/opencode.json, CLAUDE.md) only its own entries go. --only plugin/<name> removes one item; --only-runtime removes just the MCP entries.

docs.title: An Environment is not listed
docs.text: You do not have access to it. Signing in again does not help: a platform admin grants it by adding one of your teams to that Environment. If you were just added to a single sign-on group, run ach-cli refresh and wait a few minutes.
